messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer reported that in the Console some projects still show the Edit button for viewers after the RBAC refactor. Screenshot attached: https://files.redwood.example/snap/issue123.png

sam: ugh. repro steps? which project / account tier?

maria: small org on Dedicated. Steps: login as user with role=viewer, open Project Settings -> you can click Edit on environments list. Doesn't actually save, but UI enables the button.

alexa: can you paste the exact permission check we call in the frontend?

maria: frontend calls `canEditProject(user, project)` which defers to `/api/perm/check` with payload `{subject: user.id, resource: project.id, action: "project.edit"}`

maria: server side returns 403 when actually invoked. So it's purely a UI gating issue (missing flag) but still a serious UX + potential surface for confuse.

tim: looks like the role-mapping middleware we shipped last week changed the client-side feature flags shape. Frontend expects `perms.edit_project` but backend sends `permissions.project_edit` now. :facepalm:

sam: that mismatch explains it. Any sign of exploitable path? can a viewer trigger an API that actually edits something?

maria: audited the API logs: no `project.update` APIs were accepted for viewer tokens. Audit entries show `rbac.check` fail before handler. Example audit line (redacted):
```
2024-05-12T15:42:03Z | rbac.check | subject=acct:user:U123 | resource=proj:P789 | action=project.edit | result=DENY | policy_version=v2.1
```

ops-bot: deploy #deploy-frontend-2024-05-12 completed to canary (sha:abc123) :white_check_mark:

sam: quick fix options: 1) emergency frontend hotfix to use both flag shapes, 2) backend compatibility shim that emits old key name for a release window, 3) toggle-off the Edit button globally via a feature flag while we patch. Thoughts?

alexa: prefer backend shim + one release with both keys. Less UI churn for customers.

tim: agree with backend shim. Also want an audit log entry to track users who saw the Edit button (for support). We don't currently log client-side UI exposures.

maria: we can add a lightweight `ui.exposure` audit event from the client that goes to the audit pipeline. payload: `{subject, resource, exposure: "edit_button_visible", server_ts}`. That'll let support correlate.

sam: okay. timeline? can we ship shim + logging in next patch window?

ops-bot: staging build queued (job: frontend-compat) — ETA ~45m

maria: also cross-check KMS logs — some customers on Dedicated have rotated keys last week; want to ensure no mapping collision between key metadata and role map. I scanned KMS audit: nothing suspicious but leaving note.

alexa: good call. @tim can you confirm KMS metadata not used as role identifier anywhere? we had a weird migration script that tagged projects with `kms:key_id` -> maybe that script touched RBAC metadata?

tim: confirmed: the migration only touched project metadata and a `service_labels` field. RBAC uses `role_id` strings. No overlap. KMS audit excerpt: 
```
2024-05-11T03:12:54Z | kms.rotate | key_id=k-9a3f | user=ops@redwood | result=SUCCESS
```

maria: ok. so plan: roll backend shim emitting both `permissions.project_edit` and `perms.edit_project`, add client-side `ui.exposure` event, ship small frontend patch to read either key as fallback if still needed, and create a support note.

sam: assign owners: tim -> backend shim + audit schema, maria -> client exposure event + support note, sam -> coordinate deploys.

maria: created ticket INF-3482 with the plan, linking the logs and repro steps: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3482

alexa: also add a line to release notes: "UI: fixed Edit button visibility for Viewer role in Project Settings"

maria: I'll add the note. any objections to shipping shim today?

tim: no objections. make it behind a kill-switch just in case.

sam: SGTM. I'll watch the canary and roll to prod if green. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all, will update the ticket with audit queries for support.

deploy-bot: prod deploy started (pipeline: release/compat/v1.2.9)

sam: ping here if any error spikes, otherwise close after 24h of no regressions.
